quotes.text: "Well, so we did. So we always do. I'm glad your dreams could take even that much trouble about us."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "And I dreamt that Joe Harper's mother was here."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Why, she was here! Did you dream any more?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, lots. But it's so dim, now."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Well, try to recollect-- can't you?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Somehow it seems to me that the wind-- the wind blowed the-- the -- "
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Try harder, Tom! The wind did blow something. Come!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I've got it now! I've got it now! It blowed the candle!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Mercy on us! Go on, Tom-- go on!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "And it seems to me that you said, 'Why, I believe that that door-- '"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Go ON, Tom!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Just let me study a moment-- just a moment. Oh, yes-- you said you believed the door was open."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "As I'm sitting here, I did! Didn't I, Mary! Go on!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "And then-- and then-- well I won't be certain, but it seems like as if you made Sid go and-- and -- "
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Well? Well? What did I make him do, Tom? What did I make him do?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "You made him-- you-- Oh, you made him shut it."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Well, for the land's sake! I never heard the beat of that in all my days! Don't tell ME there ain't anything in dreams, any more. Sereny Harper shall know of this before I'm an hour older. I'd like to see her get around THIS with her rubbage 'bout superstition. Go on, Tom!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, it's all getting just as bright as day, now. Next you said I warn't BAD, only mischeevous and harum-scarum, and not any more responsible than-- than -- I think it was a colt, or something."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "And so it was! Well, goodness gracious! Go on, Tom!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "And then you began to cry."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "So I did. So I did. Not the first time, neither. And then -- "
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Then Mrs. Harper she began to cry, and said Joe was just the same, and she wished she hadn't whipped him for taking cream when she'd throwed it out her own self -- "
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Tom! The sperrit was upon you! You was a prophesying-- that's what you was doing! Land alive, go on, Tom!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Then Sid he said-- he said -- "
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I don't think I said anything,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Yes you did, Sid,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Shut your heads and let Tom go on! What did he say, Tom?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "He said -- I THINK he said he hoped I was better off where I was gone to, but if I'd been better sometimes -- "
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "THERE, d'you hear that! It was his very words!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "And you shut him up sharp."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I lay I did! There must 'a' been an angel there. There WAS an angel there, somewheres!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "And Mrs. Harper told about Joe scaring her with a firecracker, and you told about Peter and the Painkiller -- "
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Just as true as I live!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "And then there was a whole lot of talk 'bout dragging the river for us, and 'bout having the funeral Sunday, and then you and old Miss Harper hugged and cried, and she went."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It happened just so! It happened just so, as sure as I'm a-sitting in these very tracks. Tom, you couldn't told it more like if you'd 'a' seen it! And then what? Go on, Tom!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Then I thought you prayed for me-- and I could see you and hear every word you said. And you went to bed, and I was so sorry that I took and wrote on a piece of sycamore bark, 'We ain't dead-- we are only off being pirates,' and put it on the table by the candle; and then you looked so good, laying there asleep, that I thought I went and leaned over and kissed you on the lips."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Did you, Tom, DID you! I just forgive you everything for that!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It was very kind, even though it was only a-- dream,"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Shut up, Sid! A body does just the same in a dream as he'd do if he was awake. Here's a big Milum apple I've been saving for you, Tom, if you was ever found again-- now go 'long to school. I'm thankful to the good God and Father of us all I've got you back, that's long-suffering and merciful to them that believe on Him and keep His word, though goodness knows I'm unworthy of it, but if only the worthy ones got His blessings and had His hand to help them over the rough places, there's few enough would smile here or ever enter into His rest when the long night comes. Go 'long Sid, Mary, Tom-- take yourselves off-- you've hendered me long enough."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Pretty thin-- as long a dream as that, without any mistakes in it!"

quotes.text: "Any boy in the whole town but that Saint Louis smarty that thinks he dresses so fine and is aristocracy! Oh, all right, I licked you the first day you ever saw this town, mister, and I'll lick you again! You just wait till I catch you out! I'll just take and -- "

quotes.text: "Tom, I've a notion to skin you alive!"

quotes.text: "Auntie, what have I done?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Well, you've done enough. Here I go over to Sereny Harper, like an old softy, expecting I'm going to make her believe all that rubbage about that dream, when lo and behold you she'd found out from Joe that you was over here and heard all the talk we had that night. Tom, I don't know what is to become of a boy that will act like that. It makes me feel so bad to think you could let me go to Sereny Harper and make such a fool of myself and never say a word."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Auntie, I wish I hadn't done it-- but I didn't think."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, child, you never think. You never think of anything but your own selfishness. You could think to come all the way over here from Jackson's Island in the night to laugh at our troubles, and you could think to fool me with a lie about a dream; but you couldn't ever think to pity us and save us from sorrow."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Auntie, I know now it was mean, but I didn't mean to be mean. I didn't, honest. And besides, I didn't come over here to laugh at you that night."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What did you come for, then?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It was to tell you not to be uneasy about us, because we hadn't got drownded."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Tom, Tom, I would be the thankfullest soul in this world if I could believe you ever had as good a thought as that, but you know you never did-- and I know it, Tom."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Indeed and 'deed I did, auntie -- I wish I may never stir if I didn't."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Oh, Tom, don't lie-- don't do it. It only makes things a hundred times worse."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It ain't a lie, auntie; it's the truth. I wanted to keep you from grieving-- that was all that made me come."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I'd give the whole world to believe that-- it would cover up a power of sins, Tom. I'd 'most be glad you'd run off and acted so bad. But it ain't reasonable; because, why didn't you tell me, child?"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Why, you see, when you got to talking about the funeral, I just got all full of the idea of our coming and hiding in the church, and I couldn't somehow bear to spoil it. So I just put the bark back in my pocket and kept mum."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "What bark?"

quotes.text: "The bark I had wrote on to tell you we'd gone pirating. I wish, now, you'd waked up when I kissed you -- I do, honest."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "DID you kiss me, Tom?"

quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "Kiss me again, Tom!-- and be off with you to school, now, and don't bother me any more."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "No, I don't dare. Poor boy, I reckon he's lied about it-- but it's a blessed, blessed lie, there's such a comfort come from it. I hope the Lord -- I KNOW the Lord will forgive him, because it was such goodheartedness in him to tell it. But I don't want to find out it's a lie. I won't look."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "It's a good lie-- it's a good lie -- I won't let it grieve me."
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I could forgive the boy, now, if he'd committed a million sins!"
quotes.speaker: Unknown

quotes.text: "I acted mighty mean to-day, Becky, and I'm so sorry. I won't ever, ever do that way again, as long as ever I live-- please make up, won't you?"

quotes.text: "What a curious kind of a fool a girl is! Never been licked in school! Shucks! What's a licking! That's just like a girl-- they're so thin-skinned and chicken-hearted. Well, of course I ain't going to tell old Dobbins on this little fool, because there's other ways of getting even on her, that ain't so mean; but what of it? Old Dobbins will ask who it was tore his book. Nobody'll answer. Then he'll do just the way he always does-- ask first one and then t'other, and when he comes to the right girl he'll know it, without any telling. Girls' faces always tell on them. They ain't got any backbone. She'll get licked. Well, it's a kind of a tight place for Becky Thatcher, because there ain't any way out of it."
quotes.speaker: Unknown
